# enlace_connector

Deploy Python functions as **authenticated MCP connectors** on an
[enlace](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace) platform — so Claude.ai (and any MCP
host) can call them.

A Claude.ai “custom connector” is a remote MCP server. `enlace_connector` wraps your
tool functions with [`py2mcp`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/py2mcp), plugs auth into
the platform’s [`enlace_auth`](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace_auth) OAuth server,
and follows enlace’s app conventions so deployment is one declaration.

```python
from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec, make_connector_app, scaffold_app

spec = ConnectorSpec(
    name="trufflepig",
    tools=["truffle.mcp:search_trufflepig", "truffle.mcp:search_wallow"],
    auth="enlace",                 # validate tokens issued by the platform's enlace_auth
    extras=["truffle"],            # what the connector's own venv must install
)

# Develop locally (stdio, no auth) — Claude Desktop / Claude Code:
make_stdio_server(spec).run()

# The hosted ASGI app (Streamable HTTP + OAuth) a server runs:
app = make_connector_app(spec, issuer="https://apps.thorwhalen.com")

# Or scaffold an enlace mode=process app dir (own venv for heavy deps):
scaffold_app(spec, "tw_platform/apps/trufflepig_mcp", port=8030)
```

## Why a separate venv (`mode="process"`)

A connector with heavy dependencies (ML models, large libraries) runs as an enlace
`mode="process"` app: enlace spawns it as a supervised subprocess in its **own venv**
and reverse-proxies the route to it — keeping those deps out of the shared platform
backend. The connector validates bearer tokens itself, so enlace treats it as
`access="public"` (no session gate).

## Auth is pluggable

The connector is an OAuth 2.1 *resource server* — it validates the bearer JWTs an
authorization server issued. Who that AS is is just config:

| `auth=`             | Authorization server                      | Use                                          |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `"enlace"`          | the platform’s `enlace_auth` OAuth server | self-contained platform auth                 |
| `idp_resource(...)` | a managed IdP (Auth0, WorkOS, …)          | offload OAuth to a vendor                    |
| `None` / `"none"`   | —                                         | local stdio / unauthenticated internal pilot |

The resource-server validation is identical regardless — picking an AS doesn’t change
the connector, only where the token comes from.

## Usage logging is a switch, not code

A deployed connector otherwise leaves only the web server’s access log. With
[`py2mcp`’s usage logger](https://github.com/i2mint/py2mcp) (its ADR-0001) the
connector can keep one record per tool call — time, caller from the OAuth token,
tool, arguments, outcome, result size, latency — and one flagged record per
handshake, so “enabled” and “used” stop looking the same. **It is off by default.**
The host switches it on with environment variables (the unit file’s
`Environment=` lines), never by editing connector code:

| Variable                             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR`            | **absolute** directory for the day files, one per connector; **unset = off**. Use the connector’s own data root, off the deploy tree (a relative path is refused) |
| `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | days to keep (default 90; `0` keeps today only; `none` keeps all)                                                                                                 |
| `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_REDACT`         | comma-separated argument names to mask (error text is dropped too, since it echoes arguments)                                                                     |
| `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_ARGS`           | `0` to drop the arguments entirely                                                                                                                                |

`make_connector_app(spec)` reads them itself; a connector that builds `FastMCP`
by hand passes `middleware=usage_middleware(spec)` (an empty list when off). The
spec’s `version` and `usage_outcome` (a `"module:function"` ref to the connector’s
own `(tool, result) -> label | mapping` classifier, e.g. one that knows the search
tool’s “no match” shape) travel into the records.
The rendered systemd unit ships the `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR` line commented
out. The arguments are the users’ own questions: tell them before you turn it on,
and read the log with `py2mcp usage <dir>`.

## Deploy the whole bundle

`generate_deploy_bundle(spec, dest)` writes everything a `mode="process"` connector
needs — the app dir (`app.toml` + `server.py`), a **systemd unit** (runs it in its
own venv), a **provisioning script** (build that venv + install `extras`/`git_installs`

+ create `data` dirs + `post_install`), the two **`platform.toml` fragments**
  (`oauth-server.toml` — session longevity; `allowlist.toml` — from `allowed_users`),
  and a **runbook**. `allowed_users` is required: the platform refuses every account
  for a resource it does not list, so an empty list raises instead of deploying a
  connector nobody can authorize. `allowed_users=["*"]` opens it to every
  authenticated platform account, and has to be written out:

```python
spec = ConnectorSpec(
    name="acme", tools=["acme.mcp:search"], route="/api/acme_mcp", port=8031,
    extras=["ir", "sentence-transformers"], git_installs=["git+ssh://git@github.com/acme/acme"],
    data=[("~/.local/share/ir/corpora/acme", "{base}/xdg-data/ir/corpora/acme")],
    env={"XDG_DATA_HOME": "{base}/xdg-data", "HF_HOME": "{base}/hf-cache"},
    allowed_users=["a@acme.com", "b@acme.com"],
)
generate_deploy_bundle(spec, "apps/acme_mcp")   # → app dir + deploy/{unit,provision,toml fragments,runbook}
```

Platform specifics (paths, origin) are parameters with tw_platform defaults; the
package stays connector-type-agnostic (it knows nothing of `ir`).

### Hosts that keep their own unit files

A host may hand-maintain its units rather than install the rendered one. The spec can still describe such a unit: `app_dir` names the directory under `apps/` and `connectors/` (e.g. `"acme_mcp"`, when it is not the spec’s `name`), `environment_files` and `exec_start_pre` scope provider secrets into the process, `uvicorn_args` adds flags such as `--no-access-log`, and `service_directives` carries any other `[Service]` line (`RuntimeDirectory=`, …). Then make drift visible instead of silent:

```python
from enlace_connector import check_distinct_specs, diff_unit

check_distinct_specs(specs)          # same port (it has a default), unit name or directory: refused
for spec in specs:
    for line in diff_unit(spec, installed_unit_text(spec)):
        print(spec.name, line)       # e.g. "[Service] Environment CONNECTOR_AUDIENCE: installed lacks it"
```

`diff_unit` compares semantically (comments, directive order, whitespace and `Environment=` quoting do not count; the order of repeated `ExecStartPre=` lines does) and ignores `Description=`. It reads `Environment=` as systemd does (quotes anywhere in a word, C escapes such as `\\` and `\x41` inside quotes too) and skips comment lines inside a backslash continuation. It reads the main unit file only, not drop-ins.

## Extra routes, lifespans and an authorization gate

A connector bound to a project often needs more than tools: an extra route next to the MCP endpoint (signed downloads), startup/shutdown work of its own, and an authorization gate that must run before metering. The spec carries all three, so `make_connector_app` (and the rendered `server.py`) still builds it:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec, chain_lifespan

# acme/serve.py
def authz(server):                       # a server hook may return middleware it owns
    return ProjectGate(project="acme")   # it runs before every other middleware

@asynccontextmanager
async def signer(app):
    yield {"signer": make_signer()}      # merged into request.state

def downloads(app, server):              # an app wrapper: fn(app, server) -> app
    app.mount("/downloads", downloads_app)
    return chain_lifespan(app, signer)   # add to the app's lifespan, never replace it

spec = ConnectorSpec(
    name="acme", tools=["acme.mcp:search"], middleware=["acme.meter:gate"],
    server_hooks=["acme.serve:authz"], app_wrappers=["acme.serve:downloads"],
)
```

The app’s own lifespan runs FastMCP’s session manager, so a wrapper that replaced it would leave the MCP endpoint dead; `chain_lifespan` starts the extra work after it and stops it before. A mounted route is outside the connector’s OAuth and middleware, so it authorizes its own requests (a signature on the download link, say). The full order (hooks, then middleware outermost to innermost: hook-returned authorization, the host’s `middleware=`, the spec’s `middleware`, the usage logger; then the wrappers) is written down once, under “Serving order” in the `enlace_connector.connector` module docstring.

## Verify before you call it deployed

A connector can be perfectly healthy and completely dead to its users. If the
platform’s authorization server does not advertise the **`refresh_token` grant**,
every client session dies at the first access-token expiry (typically one hour) and
only a human re-running the interactive browser authorization can bring it back —
while the process stays up, the port answers, and nothing errors anywhere. It has
happened; the first signal was a person saying the connector had been down all day.

So the deployment isn’t good until the *authorization server* is checked:

```bash
python -m enlace_connector.preflight https://apps.thorwhalen.com   # exit 1 if it would strand
```

```python
from enlace_connector import verify_deployment, format_report

results = verify_deployment(spec, issuer="https://apps.thorwhalen.com")
print(format_report(results))
assert all(results)          # or pass strict=True to raise
```

It fetches `{issuer}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and asserts what the
**deployed** server advertises — config claiming refresh is enabled is not evidence,
since the running build may predate the feature. Checks are plain callables of a
`PreflightContext` (`checks=` to extend or replace them) and the HTTP fetcher is a
parameter (`fetch=`), so this is testable offline and CI-friendly.

Configure it from the start too: `deploy/oauth-server.toml` in the bundle carries the
`[auth.oauth_server] refresh_token_ttl_seconds` key (30 days by default; `0` disables
the grant), so a **new** platform doesn’t inherit a stranding default.

## Cost / LLM note

A connector over `ir`’s core search is **offline and free**: no LLM, no tokens.
An *agentic* connector (query reformulation, LLM selection, synopsis) needs an LLM,
which is an injected `prompt -> str` callable. `llm_tool` wraps such a tool so it
brings its own, per request:

```python
from enlace_connector import llm_tool

@llm_tool(fallback="mypkg.llm:chat")      # optional: a prompt -> str to use instead
def search(query: str, limit: int = 5, *, llm=None) -> list[dict]:
    ...                                    # llm is None: run the offline search
```

The LLM is the **client’s model via MCP sampling** when the client advertises it
(`ctx.sample`, so no metered key), else the `fallback` (a key-backed callable, or
`coact.resolve_llm()` on a developer machine), else `None` and the tool runs offline.
A sampling request that fails mid-call reruns the tool on the fallback, so the
connector never hard-fails for want of an LLM (the rerun starts the tool over, so it
must be safe to run twice up to its first LLM call). Reference the wrapped function in
the spec’s `tools` as usual. Sampling needs a stateful session: set
`stateless_http=False` on the spec, since a stateless request never sees the client’s
capabilities.

**Client support, checked 2026-10:** Claude’s MCP client (claude.ai, Desktop, mobile,
Cowork, Claude Code) lists sampling among the MCP features it does not yet support
([Build an MCP server for Claude](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/index)),
so under Claude a wrapped tool runs on its fallback or offline today. Clients that do
sample get it with no change. See `ir`’s `ir_10` note.

## Status

The connector factory, auth, **scaffolding, and full deploy-bundle generation** are
stable and tested; `auth="enlace"` is live in production. A spec carries what used to
force a hand-written `server.py`: `icon`, `instructions`, `middleware`, `server_hooks`
(tools that are not `module:function` refs, and an authorization gate) and `app_wrappers` (extra routes, lifespans). `instructions` and `version` may be
`"module:ATTR"` refs (e.g. `"mypkg.prompts:INSTRUCTIONS"`, `"mypkg:__version__"`), and
`version_dist="mypkg"` reads the installed distribution’s version, so neither is a
frozen copy that drifts from the package. Building the connector app directly is still
possible — see the `server_py=` override on `generate_deploy_bundle`.

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest -q
```

# _autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md

# enlace_connector.auth

Auth configuration for connectors — the resource-server side of MCP OAuth.

A Claude.ai custom connector is an OAuth 2.1 **resource server**: it validates the
bearer JWTs an authorization server issued (it never issues tokens itself). This
module produces the auth-config dict `py2mcp.http.mk_http_app()` consumes — a
`JWTVerifier` bound to a JWKS URI, an issuer, and an audience (the connector’s own
URL, per RFC 8707 resource indicators).

The *authorization server* is pluggable, but the resource-server config is the same
shape regardless of who issues the token — so picking an AS is just config:

- [`enlace_resource()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.enlace_resource) — the platform’s own `enlace_auth` OAuth server (the
  endpoints follow the [`ENLACE_OAUTH_PATH`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.ENLACE_OAUTH_PATH) convention this package and
  `enlace_auth` share).
- [`idp_resource()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.idp_resource) — an external managed IdP (Auth0, WorkOS, …): pass its
  `jwks_uri` / `issuer` explicitly.
- `None` / `"none"` — unauthenticated (local stdio, or an internal pilot).

### Module Attributes

| [`ENLACE_OAUTH_PATH`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.ENLACE_OAUTH_PATH)   | Path under the platform origin where `enlace_auth` serves its OAuth 2.1 authorization-server endpoints (authorize / token / register / jwks).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_SCOPES`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.DFLT_SCOPES)         | Default OAuth scopes a connector requires (read-only retrieval).                                                                                |

### Functions

| [`enlace_resource`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.enlace_resource)(\*, issuer, audience[, ...])   | Resource-server config validating tokens from the platform's `enlace_auth` AS.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`idp_resource`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.idp_resource)(\*, jwks_uri, issuer, audience)   | Resource-server config validating tokens from an external managed IdP.           |
| [`resolve_auth`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.resolve_auth)(auth, \*[, issuer, audience])     | Normalize an `auth` spec to a py2mcp auth dict (or `None` for no auth).          |

### enlace_connector.auth.DFLT_SCOPES *= ('mcp:read',)*

Default OAuth scopes a connector requires (read-only retrieval).

### enlace_connector.auth.ENLACE_OAUTH_PATH *= '/auth/oauth'*

Path under the platform origin where `enlace_auth` serves its OAuth 2.1
authorization-server endpoints (authorize / token / register / jwks). The
AS *issuer* is the bare platform origin; discovery lives at the standard
`{issuer}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. This constant is the
single source of truth shared with `enlace_auth` so the two never drift.

### enlace_connector.auth.enlace_resource(, issuer, audience, scopes=('mcp:read',), mcp_path='/mcp')

Resource-server config validating tokens from the platform’s `enlace_auth` AS.

* **Parameters:**
  * **issuer** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the platform origin acting as the OAuth issuer, e.g.
    `"https://apps.thorwhalen.com"` (no trailing slash needed).
  * **audience** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – this connector’s **base** URL (e.g.
    `"https://apps.thorwhalen.com/api/trufflepig_mcp"`).
  * **scopes** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – scopes the connector requires (default [`DFLT_SCOPES`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.DFLT_SCOPES)).
  * **mcp_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the MCP transport sub-path (FastMCP default `/mcp`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The OAuth *resource* a connector validates is its MCP **endpoint**
(`base + mcp_path`) — that is what FastMCP advertises in the RFC 9728
protected-resource metadata, and therefore what the issued token’s `aud`
carries. So `base_url` (used to build that metadata) is the base, while the
validated `audience` is `base + mcp_path`. Setting them equal causes an
“audience mismatch” 401 at token-validation time.

### enlace_connector.auth.idp_resource(, jwks_uri, issuer, audience, authorization_servers=None, base_url=None, scopes=('mcp:read',))

Resource-server config validating tokens from an external managed IdP.

Everything is explicit because each IdP (Auth0, WorkOS, Okta…) publishes its
own `jwks_uri` / `issuer`. `authorization_servers` defaults to
`[issuer]` and `base_url` to `audience` (this connector’s URL).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### enlace_connector.auth.resolve_auth(auth, , issuer=None, audience=None)

Normalize an `auth` spec to a py2mcp auth dict (or `None` for no auth).

Accepts:

- `None` or `"none"` → unauthenticated (returns `None`).
- a ready auth dict → returned unchanged.
- `"enlace"` → [`enlace_resource()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.enlace_resource) (needs *issuer* and *audience*).
- `"idp"` → not resolvable from a bare string; pass an explicit dict from
  [`idp_resource()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.auth.html.md#enlace_connector.auth.idp_resource) instead (raises with that guidance).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md

# enlace_connector.connector

Define a connector once, run it anywhere — stdio (local) or HTTP (hosted).

A [`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec) is the single declaration of a connector: the Python tool
functions to expose, the auth strategy, the public route, and the pip extras its
runtime venv needs. The factories turn that one spec into the artifacts each host
wants:

- [`make_stdio_server()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_stdio_server) — a FastMCP server for Claude Desktop / Claude Code while
  developing (no auth).
- [`make_connector_app()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_connector_app) — the Streamable-HTTP ASGI app an enlace platform mounts
  (or a standalone ASGI server runs) — with auth resolved from the spec.

Tools are given as `"module:function"` reference strings (py2mcp’s form), so the
spec is import-light and serializable — the heavy tool modules load only in the
process that actually serves them.

## Serving order

This is the one place the order is written down; every other docstring points here.
[`make_connector_app()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_connector_app) builds a connector in these steps:

1. **Server.** The FastMCP server is built from the spec’s `tools`, `icon` and
   `instructions`, with the middleware stack of step 3.
2. **Server hooks.** Each `server_hooks` ref is called as `hook(server)`, in
   order. A hook may add tools, and it may **return** middleware (one, or a
   list or tuple of them): that middleware is the builder’s own (an
   authorization gate bound to a project) and goes to the front of the stack. Any
   other return value (`None`, the tool `server.tool` gave back) adds none; a
   list or tuple holding anything but middleware is refused.
3. **Middleware**, outermost (runs first on a call) to innermost:
   1. what the server hooks returned, in hook order (authorization);
   2. the host’s `middleware=` argument to [`make_connector_app()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_connector_app);
   3. the spec’s `middleware` refs, in order (e.g. a metering gate);
   4. the usage logger, when the host switched it on ([`usage`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#module-enlace_connector.usage)).

   So a call is authorized before it is metered, and metered before it is logged
   as usage: a refused call is never counted or logged. Middleware a hook adds
   itself with `server.add_middleware` lands after all of these.
4. **ASGI app.** `server.http_app(...)` gives the Starlette app; its lifespan
   runs FastMCP’s session manager.
5. **App wrappers.** Each `app_wrappers` ref is called as
   `wrapper(app, server) -> app`, in order, each on the previous one’s result
   (an extra mount, CORS, …). A wrapper with startup/shutdown work of its own
   chains it onto the app’s lifespan with [`chain_lifespan()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.chain_lifespan), never in place
   of it: replacing it stops the session manager and the MCP endpoint fails.
   A route a wrapper mounts is **not** behind the connector’s OAuth (that guards
   the MCP route only) nor its middleware (that sees MCP calls only): it does its
   own authorization, e.g. by checking a signature on a signed download link.

[`make_stdio_server()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_stdio_server) runs steps 1 and 2 only: there is no stack (the
middleware is the hosted path’s gating and metering) and no ASGI app, so what a
hook returns is ignored there.

### Functions

| [`make_stdio_server`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_stdio_server)(spec)                     | Build a FastMCP server for *spec*, for local stdio serving (no auth).                                                    |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_connector_app`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_connector_app)(spec, \*[, issuer, ...]) | Build the Streamable-HTTP ASGI app for *spec* (the hosted connector).                                                    |
| [`chain_lifespan`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.chain_lifespan)(app, extra_lifespan)         | Run *extra_lifespan* inside *app*'s own lifespan, and return *app*.                                                      |
| [`spec_instructions`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.spec_instructions)(spec)                     | *spec*'s instructions, a `"module:ATTR"` ref resolved to its text.                                                       |
| [`spec_version`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.spec_version)(spec)                          | *spec*'s version: `version` (a `"module:ATTR"` ref resolved), else the installed version of `version_dist`, else `None`. |

### Classes

| [`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec)(name, tools[, auth, title, ...])   | A declarative connector definition (see the module docstring).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec(name, tools, auth='enlace', title=None, route=None, extras=list(), git_installs=list(), port=8030, data=list(), env=dict(), allowed_users=list(), post_install=list(), stateless_http=True, version=None, version_dist=None, usage_outcome=None, app_dir=None, environment_files=list(), exec_start_pre=list(), uvicorn_args=list(), service_directives=list(), icon=None, instructions=None, middleware=list(), server_hooks=list(), app_wrappers=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A declarative connector definition (see the module docstring).

#### name

short identifier — the enlace app name and default route stem.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### tools

`"module:function"` refs exposed as MCP tools.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

Defaults to `"enlace"` — the platform’s own OAuth server.

human-facing MCP server name (defaults to *name*).

enlace mount route (defaults to `"/{name}-mcp"`).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### extras

PyPI requirements the connector’s own runtime venv needs (e.g. the
package owning the tools + its embedder deps).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### git_installs

non-PyPI deps as pip specs (e.g.
`"git+ssh://git@github.com/org/pkg"`) for private/unreleased packages.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### port

the fixed local port the connector process binds; enlace reverse-
proxies the route to `127.0.0.1:{port}`. Must be free on the box.

* **Type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### data

`(local_path, remote_path)` pairs to co-locate on the server —
large artifacts (corpus stores, model caches) shipped *separately* from
code (rsynced), the deploy runbook lists the copy step.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

#### env

environment variables the connector’s systemd unit sets (e.g.
`XDG_DATA_HOME` / `HF_HOME` pointing at the `data` dirs).

* **Type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### allowed_users

emails permitted to authorize this connector — becomes the
platform’s `[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` entry. Required
for a deploy bundle: enlace_auth refuses every account for a resource
it does not list (fail closed, since enlace_auth 0.1.30), so an empty
list is an error, never “open”. `["*"]` (`deploy.ANY_ACCOUNT`)
admits every authenticated platform account, and must be written out.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### post_install

shell commands run *inside the connector venv* after deps
install (e.g. pre-warming an embedding model so the first query
doesn’t block). `{venv}` / `{base}` placeholders are substituted.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### stateless_http

run the MCP transport statelessly (recommended behind a
multi-worker server / load balancer). Defaults to True.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### version

the connector’s version, written into every usage-log record
when logging is on (see [`enlace_connector.usage`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#module-enlace_connector.usage)). A
`"module:ATTR"` ref (e.g. `"mypkg:__version__"`) is imported where
the connector is served, so the version is never a frozen copy.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### version_dist

the installed distribution whose version is the
connector’s (`importlib.metadata.version`), used when *version* is
not set — the seam for packages without a `__version__`.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### usage_outcome

a `"module:function"` ref to this connector’s own
`(tool_name, result) -> label | mapping` usage-outcome classifier
(e.g. one that knows the search tool’s “no match” shape), used in
place of py2mcp’s generic one when logging is on.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### app_dir

the connector’s directory name under the platform’s `apps/`
and `connectors/` (defaults to *name*). A host that names the app
`<name>_mcp` sets it so the rendered paths exist (#15).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### environment_files

`EnvironmentFile=` values for the unit, in order —
how a host scopes provider secrets into the process without writing
them into the unit. A leading `-` makes one optional, as in systemd.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### exec_start_pre

`ExecStartPre=` commands, in order (e.g. extracting the
scoped secrets an `environment_files` entry then reads).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### uvicorn_args

extra arguments appended to the `uvicorn` command line
(e.g. `--no-access-log` for a connector that serves signed links).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### service_directives

any other `(key, value)` lines for the unit’s
`[Service]` section, in order (e.g. `("RuntimeDirectory", ...)`).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

#### icon

the server icon clients show next to the connector (sent in the MCP
`serverInfo`): a `src` URL or `data:` URI, or a dict of
`mcp.types.Icon` fields (`src`, `mimeType`, `sizes`).

* **Type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### instructions

the server’s model-facing description, surfaced to the
connecting client as the MCP `instructions`. A `"module:ATTR"`
ref (dotted identifiers, no spaces) names a string in the connector’s
package instead, imported where the connector is served, so the text
lives in one place and cannot drift from a copy in the spec.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### middleware

`"module:attr"` refs to extra FastMCP middleware, in order
(e.g. a metering gate). Each names a middleware, a list of them, or a
zero-argument factory returning either. Where they sit among the
other middleware: “Serving order” in this module’s docstring.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### server_hooks

`"module:function"` refs, each called with the built
FastMCP server before it is served — the seam for tools that are not
importable `"module:function"` refs (closures bound to a project, a
store, a per-caller context): `server.tool(fn)` inside the hook.
A hook may return middleware it owns (an authorization gate), which
runs before every other middleware (“Serving order”).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### app_wrappers

`"module:function"` refs, each called as
`wrapper(app, server) -> app` on the hosted ASGI app, in order —
the seam for an extra route next to the MCP endpoint (a mount for
signed downloads) and its own startup/shutdown work, which goes
through [`chain_lifespan()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.chain_lifespan). Hosted path only. A mounted route
is outside the connector’s OAuth and middleware (“Serving order”).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### The last four take the same \`\`{base}\`\` / \`\`{venv}\`\` / \`\`{app_dir}\`\` /

### \`\`{remote_base}\`\` / \`\`{name}\`\` / \`\`{port}\`\` placeholders as \*env\*.

### Unlike \*env\*, a \`\`%\`\` in them is written as-is, so systemd specifiers

### (\`\`%t\`\`, \`\`%n\`\`) work there; write \`\`%%\`\` for a literal one.

#### default_audience(platform_origin)

This connector’s public URL under *platform_origin* (the token audience).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### *property* dir_name *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The directory name under `apps/` and `connectors/` (see *app_dir*).

#### *property* mount_route *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

one leading `/`, no trailing `/`.

`"/x/"` and `"x"` both mean `"/x"`. Everything that names the connector
(its token audience, its allowlist key, its `app.toml` route) derives from
this, so a stray slash cannot make two of them disagree (#10).

* **Type:**
  The route, spelled one way

### enlace_connector.connector.chain_lifespan(app, extra_lifespan)

Run *extra_lifespan* inside *app*’s own lifespan, and return *app*.

*app* is a Starlette app (what `server.http_app(...)` returns); its own
lifespan runs FastMCP’s session manager, so an app wrapper that needs
startup/shutdown work must add to it, not replace it (see “Serving order” in
the module docstring). *extra_lifespan* is a Starlette lifespan: a callable
taking the app and returning an async context manager (an
`@asynccontextmanager` function), or an async generator function taking the
app, as Starlette’s `lifespan=` accepts. It starts after the app’s own
lifespan and stops before it, so the MCP endpoint is up for as long as the
extra work is. If either yields a state mapping, the two are merged (the
extra one wins on a shared key) into the request `scope["state"]`; that
needs an ASGI server with lifespan state (uvicorn has it).

```pycon
>>> from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
>>> from starlette.applications import Starlette
>>> @asynccontextmanager
... async def downloads(app):
...     yield {"signer": "ready"}
>>> app = chain_lifespan(Starlette(), downloads)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### enlace_connector.connector.make_connector_app(spec, , issuer=None, audience=None, settings=None, middleware=None)

Build the Streamable-HTTP ASGI app for *spec* (the hosted connector).

Resolves the spec’s `auth` into a py2mcp resource-server config. For
`auth="enlace"` provide *issuer* (the platform origin) and *audience* (this
connector’s public URL); if *audience* is omitted it is derived from *issuer* +
the spec’s route. Returns an ASGI app to run under any ASGI server (or mount in
enlace). The spec’s `icon`, `instructions`, `middleware`,
`server_hooks` and `app_wrappers` are applied, so a connector that needs
them is still built here rather than by hand (#3, #22). The order they are
applied in is “Serving order” in the module docstring.

Per-call usage logging is attached when the host’s *settings* (`os.environ`
by default) set `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR` — see [`enlace_connector.usage`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#module-enlace_connector.usage);
it is off otherwise; the spec’s `version` and `usage_outcome` feed it. Any
extra *middleware* (one or an ordered iterable) runs before the spec’s and the
logger, so a gate (e.g. `enlace_metering`) refuses a call before it is logged
as usage. Do not add a second `usage_middleware(...)` there: every call would
be recorded twice.

### enlace_connector.connector.make_stdio_server(spec)

Build a FastMCP server for *spec*, for local stdio serving (no auth).

Use for `server.run()` in Claude Desktop / Claude Code while developing the
tools; the hosted path uses [`make_connector_app()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.make_connector_app). The spec’s `icon`,
`instructions` and `server_hooks` apply; its `middleware`, the
middleware its hooks return, and its `app_wrappers` do not (they are the
hosted path’s gating, metering and routes; see “Serving order” in the module
docstring).

### enlace_connector.connector.spec_instructions(spec)

*spec*’s instructions, a `"module:ATTR"` ref resolved to its text.

```pycon
>>> spec_instructions(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], instructions="Use me."))
'Use me.'
>>> spec_instructions(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[],
...                                 instructions="string:ascii_lowercase"))[:3]
'abc'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.connector.spec_version(spec)

*spec*’s version: `version` (a `"module:ATTR"` ref resolved), else the
installed version of `version_dist`, else `None`. The version is only a
label in the usage log, so a ref that does not import is kept as written and
an uninstalled `version_dist` gives `None`, each with a warning, rather
than stopping the connector at boot.

```pycon
>>> spec_version(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], version="1.2.0"))
'1.2.0'
>>> spec_version(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], version_dist="pytest")) > "0"
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md

# enlace_connector.deploy

Generate everything needed to deploy a connector on an enlace platform.

In production, enlace only *reverse-proxies* a `mode="process"` app’s route to
`127.0.0.1:{port}` — the connector’s actual process runs under a \*\*systemd
unit\*\* in its **own venv** (enlace delegates production process management to
systemd). So a full deploy is more than an `app.toml`; this module renders the
whole bundle from a [`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec):

- the **systemd unit** (runs the connector in its dedicated venv),
- the **provisioning script** (build that venv + install deps + create data dirs
  + install/start the unit — idempotent, run as root on the box),
- the **resource-allowlist** TOML fragment for `platform.toml` (access control),
- the **resource-display-names** TOML fragment (so the shared OAuth consent page
  shows *this* connector’s name, not whichever connector configured it first —
  i2mint/enlace_auth#18),
- the **\`\`[auth.oauth_server]\`\`** fragment (session longevity — a platform without
  a refresh-token TTL strands every connector at its first token expiry),
- a **runbook** listing the human steps (ship data, provision, deploy, verify).

It generalizes the artifacts first hand-written for the trufflepig connector, so
deploying the next one is `generate_deploy_bundle(spec)` + following the runbook.
Platform specifics (paths, origin) are parameters with tw_platform defaults —
`enlace_connector` stays connector-type-agnostic (it knows nothing of `ir`).

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_REMOTE_BASE`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.DFLT_REMOTE_BASE)   | Defaults for the tw_platform target (override per call for another platform).                                                      |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`MCP_PATH`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.MCP_PATH)           | FastMCP's Streamable-HTTP sub-path — the OAuth *resource* is `route + MCP_PATH`.                                                   |
| [`ANY_ACCOUNT`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.ANY_ACCOUNT)        | enlace_auth's spelling of "every authenticated account" in a resource allowlist entry (`enlace_auth.resource_policy.ANY_ACCOUNT`). |

### Functions

| [`resource_url`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.resource_url)(spec, \*[, issuer])                   | The connector's OAuth resource = its public MCP endpoint (`route + /mcp`).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`render_systemd_unit`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_systemd_unit)(spec, \*[, remote_base, ...])  | Render the systemd unit that runs the connector in its own venv.             |
| [`diff_unit`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.diff_unit)(spec, installed, \*[, remote_base, ...]) | How the *installed* unit text differs from what *spec* renders; `[]` if not. |
| [`check_distinct_ports`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.check_distinct_ports)(specs)                        | Refuse *specs* that would bind the same local port.                          |
| [`check_distinct_specs`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.check_distinct_specs)(specs)                        | Refuse *specs* that would collide on one host: same port, unit or directory. |
| [`render_provision_script`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_provision_script)(spec, \*[, remote_base])   | Render the idempotent, run-as-root provisioning script for the connector.    |
| [`render_allowlist_toml`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_allowlist_toml)(spec, \*[, issuer])          | Render the `[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` fragment.                |
| [`allowlist_users`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.allowlist_users)(spec)                              | `spec.allowed_users`, refused when it cannot mean what it seems to.          |
| [`render_display_names_toml`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_display_names_toml)(spec, \*[, issuer])      | Render the `[auth.oauth_server.resource_display_names]` fragment.            |
| [`render_oauth_server_toml`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_oauth_server_toml)(spec, \*[, issuer, ...])  | Render the `[auth.oauth_server]` fragment that keeps sessions alive.         |
| [`render_runbook`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_runbook)(spec, \*[, remote_base, issuer])    | Render the human deploy checklist (ship, provision, deploy, **verify**).     |
| [`generate_deploy_bundle`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.generate_deploy_bundle)(spec, dest, \*[, ...])      | Write the full deploy bundle for *spec* under *dest*.                        |

### enlace_connector.deploy.ANY_ACCOUNT *= '\*'*

enlace_auth’s spelling of “every authenticated account” in a resource
allowlist entry (`enlace_auth.resource_policy.ANY_ACCOUNT`).

### enlace_connector.deploy.DFLT_REMOTE_BASE *= '/opt/tw_platform'*

Defaults for the tw_platform target (override per call for another platform).

### enlace_connector.deploy.MCP_PATH *= '/mcp'*

FastMCP’s Streamable-HTTP sub-path — the OAuth *resource* is `route + MCP_PATH`.

### enlace_connector.deploy.allowlist_users(spec)

`spec.allowed_users`, refused when it cannot mean what it seems to.

enlace_auth fails closed: a resource missing from
`[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` is refused to everyone
(i2mint/enlace_auth#34). So an empty list no longer means “open”. It
would deploy a connector that nobody can authorize, and nothing would
error until someone tried (#8). Opening a connector to every account is
an explicit `["*"]`.

```pycon
>>> from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec
>>> allowlist_users(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=["m:f"], allowed_users=["*"]))
['*']
>>> allowlist_users(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=["m:f"]))
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: Connector 'x' has no allowed_users...
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### enlace_connector.deploy.check_distinct_ports(specs)

Refuse *specs* that would bind the same local port.

`port` has a default, so two specs that both omit it render units that
collide on one box, and the second connector never starts (#15). Prefer
[`check_distinct_specs()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.check_distinct_specs), which also checks unit names and directories.

```pycon
>>> check_distinct_ports([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[], port=8031),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[], port=8032)])
>>> check_distinct_ports([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[]),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[])])
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: connectors share a port: 8030 (a, b)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.deploy.check_distinct_specs(specs)

Refuse *specs* that would collide on one host: same port, unit or directory.

Run it over every connector a host deploys. Two specs collide when they bind
the same `port` (it has a default), share a `name` (one
`<name>-mcp.service`, one resource URL), or share a directory under
`apps/` and `connectors/` (`app_dir`, else `name`): the second
install would overwrite the first (#18). Every clash is listed in one error.

```pycon
>>> check_distinct_specs([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[], port=8031),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[], port=8032)])
>>> check_distinct_specs([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[], port=8031),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[], port=8032, app_dir="a")])
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: connectors share a directory: a (a, b)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.deploy.diff_unit(spec, installed, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com', ignore=frozenset({('Unit', 'Description')}))

How the *installed* unit text differs from what *spec* renders; `[]` if not.

For a host that keeps its own unit files: run it per connector at deploy time
and report the lines, so a unit and its spec cannot drift apart unnoticed
(#15). The comparison is semantic: comments, blank lines, line order across
directives, whitespace runs and `Environment=` quoting do not count; the
order of repeated directives (`ExecStartPre=`) does. *ignore* is a set of
`(section, key)` pairs left out (the `Description=` prose, by default).
Drop-ins (`<unit>.d/*.conf`) are not read: pass the main unit file.

```pycon
>>> spec = ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], port=8040)
>>> diff_unit(spec, render_systemd_unit(spec))
[]
>>> diff_unit(spec, render_systemd_unit(spec).replace("8040", "8041"))[0][:21]
'[Service] ExecStart: '
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### enlace_connector.deploy.generate_deploy_bundle(spec, dest, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com', server_py=None, refresh_token_ttl_seconds=2592000)

Write the full deploy bundle for *spec* under *dest*.

Writes the app dir (`app.toml` + `server.py`) and a `deploy/` folder (the
systemd unit, provisioning script, the `platform.toml` fragments — OAuth
session longevity, the display name and the resource allowlist — and the
runbook). Raises `ValueError`, writing nothing, when `allowed_users` is
empty (see [`allowlist_users()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.allowlist_users)). Pass *server_py* to override the generated entry module
(e.g. a corpus-bound `make_search` server the composing skill wrote); pass
*refresh_token_ttl_seconds* to set the session longevity the platform fragment
configures (`0` would disable the refresh grant — see
[`render_oauth_server_toml()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_oauth_server_toml)). Returns the written paths.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

### enlace_connector.deploy.render_allowlist_toml(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the `[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` fragment.

Maps this connector’s resource URL to the allowed emails (or `"*"`) —
paste into the platform’s `platform.toml`. Raises `ValueError` when
`allowed_users` is empty: see [`allowlist_users()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.allowlist_users).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.deploy.render_display_names_toml(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the `[auth.oauth_server.resource_display_names]` fragment.

The shared OAuth consent page (`enlace_auth`) shows *some* product name to
every user authorizing *any* connector on the platform — resolved from
`resource_display_names`, keyed by resource URL (see
[`resource_url()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.resource_url)), with a generic fallback when a resource has no entry.
Before this existed, that string had to be hand-typed once in platform
config and drifted the moment a second connector was added: every consent
screen showed the *first* connector’s name (i2mint/enlace_auth#18).

This makes `ConnectorSpec.title` the single source instead — paste the
fragment into the platform’s `platform.toml` alongside
[`render_allowlist_toml()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_allowlist_toml)’s.

```pycon
>>> from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec
>>> spec = ConnectorSpec(name="acme", tools=["m:f"], title="Acme Knowledge")
>>> print(render_display_names_toml(spec))
[auth.oauth_server.resource_display_names]
"https://apps.thorwhalen.com/acme-mcp/mcp" = "Acme Knowledge"
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.deploy.render_oauth_server_toml(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com', refresh_token_ttl_seconds=2592000)

Render the `[auth.oauth_server]` fragment that keeps sessions alive.

Companion to [`render_allowlist_toml()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.render_allowlist_toml): that one renders the
`[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` *subtable*, this one the scalar keys
of the parent table — so a **new** platform is configured for connector-length
sessions from the start instead of inheriting a default that issues no refresh
tokens. Paste this block *before* the allowlist fragment (TOML requires a
table’s own keys to precede its subtables).

```pycon
>>> from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec
>>> spec = ConnectorSpec(name="acme", tools=["m:f"])
>>> print(render_oauth_server_toml(spec))
#...
[auth.oauth_server]
refresh_token_ttl_seconds = 2592000
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.deploy.render_provision_script(spec, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform')

Render the idempotent, run-as-root provisioning script for the connector.

Builds the dedicated venv (this box’s `ensurepip` is unavailable, so
`--without-pip` + `get-pip.py`, using the same base interpreter that made
the shared venv), installs `extras` + `git_installs`, creates the data
dirs, runs `post_install` (e.g. warm a model), and installs/starts the unit.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.deploy.render_runbook(spec, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the human deploy checklist (ship, provision, deploy, **verify**).

The last step is the one that is easy to skip and expensive to skip: a
connector whose authorization server cannot issue refresh tokens looks fully
deployed and dies silently hours later, so the runbook states that failure mode
in plain words and gives the exact command that detects it.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.deploy.render_systemd_unit(spec, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the systemd unit that runs the connector in its own venv.

A host that hand-maintains its units can treat this as the reference: run
[`diff_unit()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.deploy.html.md#enlace_connector.deploy.diff_unit) against each installed unit, so the two cannot drift apart
silently (#15). The spec carries what such units need: an `app_dir` name,
`environment_files` and `exec_start_pre` for scoped secrets,
`uvicorn_args`, and other `service_directives`.

`CONNECTOR_AUDIENCE` is rendered next to `CONNECTOR_ISSUER` by the same code
that renders the allowlist key, and `render_server_py()` passes it through
explicitly, so the runtime never re-derives it: a connector venv holding an older
`enlace_connector` (whose `mount_route` spelled the route differently) still
validates tokens for exactly the key the platform allows (#12).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.deploy.resource_url(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

The connector’s OAuth resource = its public MCP endpoint (`route + /mcp`).

The result is the allowlist key, so it must be canonical: enlace_auth refuses any
other spelling at config load. The route is normalized by
`ConnectorSpec.mount_route`; an issuer that is not canonical (an uppercase
host, a default port, a path segment that is empty or a dot) is refused here
rather than lowercased, because the same issuer is the connector’s runtime
`iss`/audience origin and must be fixed at its source (#10).

```pycon
>>> resource_url(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], route="/api/x_mcp/"))
'https://apps.thorwhalen.com/api/x_mcp/mcp'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md

# enlace_connector

`enlace_connector` — deploy Python functions as authenticated MCP connectors.

A Claude.ai “custom connector” is a remote MCP server. This package turns a set of
Python functions into one — wired for the [enlace](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace)
platform and its [enlace_auth](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace_auth) OAuth server,
built on [py2mcp](https://github.com/thorwhalen/py2mcp).

Declare a connector once:

```default
from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec, make_connector_app

spec = ConnectorSpec(
    name="trufflepig",
    tools=["truffle.mcp:search_trufflepig", "truffle.mcp:search_wallow"],
    auth="enlace",                 # validate the platform's enlace_auth tokens
    extras=["truffle"],            # what the connector's runtime venv needs
)
```

…then run it where you need it:

- `make_stdio_server(spec)` → a FastMCP server for Claude Desktop / Claude Code.
- `make_connector_app(spec, issuer=...)` → the Streamable-HTTP ASGI app a host runs.
- `scaffold_app(spec, dest)` → an enlace `mode="process"` app dir (`app.toml` +
  `server.py`) so a heavy connector runs in its own venv, reverse-proxied by enlace.

Per-call usage logging (who called which tool, with what, and what came back) is
off unless the host sets `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR` (see `enlace_connector.usage`).

The authorization server is pluggable (`auth="enlace"` for the platform’s own
`enlace_auth`; `idp_resource(...)` for Auth0/WorkOS/…; `None` for an
unauthenticated local/pilot run) — the resource-server validation is identical
regardless of who issues the token.

Whichever one you point at, **verify it before calling a deployment good**:

```default
from enlace_connector import verify_deployment, format_report
print(format_report(verify_deployment(spec, issuer="https://apps.example.com")))
```

An authorization server that cannot issue refresh tokens strands every connector
session at its first access-token expiry while the connector process goes on
looking perfectly healthy — [`enlace_connector.preflight`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#module-enlace_connector.preflight) is what catches that
in seconds instead of when a user complains a day later.

### *class* enlace_connector.CheckResult(name, ok, summary, remedy='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Outcome of one preflight check.

Truthy when the check passed, so `all(results)` reads naturally.

#### name

stable slug for the check (usable as a CI job/report key).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### ok

whether the checked property holds.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### summary

one line stating what was (or was not) observed.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### remedy

what to do about it — empty when `ok`.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### *class* enlace_connector.ConnectorSpec(name, tools, auth='enlace', title=None, route=None, extras=list(), git_installs=list(), port=8030, data=list(), env=dict(), allowed_users=list(), post_install=list(), stateless_http=True, version=None, version_dist=None, usage_outcome=None, app_dir=None, environment_files=list(), exec_start_pre=list(), uvicorn_args=list(), service_directives=list(), icon=None, instructions=None, middleware=list(), server_hooks=list(), app_wrappers=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A declarative connector definition (see the module docstring).

#### name

short identifier — the enlace app name and default route stem.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### tools

`"module:function"` refs exposed as MCP tools.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### auth

`"enlace"` / `"none"` / an auth dict (e.g. from `idp_resource`).
Defaults to `"enlace"` — the platform’s own OAuth server.

* **Type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### title

human-facing MCP server name (defaults to *name*).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### route

enlace mount route (defaults to `"/{name}-mcp"`).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### extras

PyPI requirements the connector’s own runtime venv needs (e.g. the
package owning the tools + its embedder deps).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### git_installs

non-PyPI deps as pip specs (e.g.
`"git+ssh://git@github.com/org/pkg"`) for private/unreleased packages.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### port

the fixed local port the connector process binds; enlace reverse-
proxies the route to `127.0.0.1:{port}`. Must be free on the box.

* **Type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### data

`(local_path, remote_path)` pairs to co-locate on the server —
large artifacts (corpus stores, model caches) shipped *separately* from
code (rsynced), the deploy runbook lists the copy step.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

#### env

environment variables the connector’s systemd unit sets (e.g.
`XDG_DATA_HOME` / `HF_HOME` pointing at the `data` dirs).

* **Type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### allowed_users

emails permitted to authorize this connector — becomes the
platform’s `[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` entry. Required
for a deploy bundle: enlace_auth refuses every account for a resource
it does not list (fail closed, since enlace_auth 0.1.30), so an empty
list is an error, never “open”. `["*"]` (`deploy.ANY_ACCOUNT`)
admits every authenticated platform account, and must be written out.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### post_install

shell commands run *inside the connector venv* after deps
install (e.g. pre-warming an embedding model so the first query
doesn’t block). `{venv}` / `{base}` placeholders are substituted.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### stateless_http

run the MCP transport statelessly (recommended behind a
multi-worker server / load balancer). Defaults to True.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### version

the connector’s version, written into every usage-log record
when logging is on (see [`enlace_connector.usage`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#module-enlace_connector.usage)). A
`"module:ATTR"` ref (e.g. `"mypkg:__version__"`) is imported where
the connector is served, so the version is never a frozen copy.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### version_dist

the installed distribution whose version is the
connector’s (`importlib.metadata.version`), used when *version* is
not set — the seam for packages without a `__version__`.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### usage_outcome

a `"module:function"` ref to this connector’s own
`(tool_name, result) -> label | mapping` usage-outcome classifier
(e.g. one that knows the search tool’s “no match” shape), used in
place of py2mcp’s generic one when logging is on.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### app_dir

the connector’s directory name under the platform’s `apps/`
and `connectors/` (defaults to *name*). A host that names the app
`<name>_mcp` sets it so the rendered paths exist (#15).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### environment_files

`EnvironmentFile=` values for the unit, in order —
how a host scopes provider secrets into the process without writing
them into the unit. A leading `-` makes one optional, as in systemd.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### exec_start_pre

`ExecStartPre=` commands, in order (e.g. extracting the
scoped secrets an `environment_files` entry then reads).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### uvicorn_args

extra arguments appended to the `uvicorn` command line
(e.g. `--no-access-log` for a connector that serves signed links).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### service_directives

any other `(key, value)` lines for the unit’s
`[Service]` section, in order (e.g. `("RuntimeDirectory", ...)`).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

#### icon

the server icon clients show next to the connector (sent in the MCP
`serverInfo`): a `src` URL or `data:` URI, or a dict of
`mcp.types.Icon` fields (`src`, `mimeType`, `sizes`).

* **Type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### instructions

the server’s model-facing description, surfaced to the
connecting client as the MCP `instructions`. A `"module:ATTR"`
ref (dotted identifiers, no spaces) names a string in the connector’s
package instead, imported where the connector is served, so the text
lives in one place and cannot drift from a copy in the spec.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### middleware

`"module:attr"` refs to extra FastMCP middleware, in order
(e.g. a metering gate). Each names a middleware, a list of them, or a
zero-argument factory returning either. Where they sit among the
other middleware: “Serving order” in this module’s docstring.

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### server_hooks

`"module:function"` refs, each called with the built
FastMCP server before it is served — the seam for tools that are not
importable `"module:function"` refs (closures bound to a project, a
store, a per-caller context): `server.tool(fn)` inside the hook.
A hook may return middleware it owns (an authorization gate), which
runs before every other middleware (“Serving order”).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### app_wrappers

`"module:function"` refs, each called as
`wrapper(app, server) -> app` on the hosted ASGI app, in order —
the seam for an extra route next to the MCP endpoint (a mount for
signed downloads) and its own startup/shutdown work, which goes
through [`chain_lifespan()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.chain_lifespan). Hosted path only. A mounted route
is outside the connector’s OAuth and middleware (“Serving order”).

* **Type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### The last four take the same \`\`{base}\`\` / \`\`{venv}\`\` / \`\`{app_dir}\`\` /

### \`\`{remote_base}\`\` / \`\`{name}\`\` / \`\`{port}\`\` placeholders as \*env\*.

### Unlike \*env\*, a \`\`%\`\` in them is written as-is, so systemd specifiers

### (\`\`%t\`\`, \`\`%n\`\`) work there; write \`\`%%\`\` for a literal one.

#### default_audience(platform_origin)

This connector’s public URL under *platform_origin* (the token audience).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### *property* dir_name *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The directory name under `apps/` and `connectors/` (see *app_dir*).

#### *property* mount_route *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

one leading `/`, no trailing `/`.

`"/x/"` and `"x"` both mean `"/x"`. Everything that names the connector
(its token audience, its allowlist key, its `app.toml` route) derives from
this, so a stray slash cannot make two of them disagree (#10).

* **Type:**
  The route, spelled one way

### *class* enlace_connector.PreflightContext(issuer, spec=None, fetch=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a check is given: the target AS, the connector (if any), and a fetcher.

#### issuer

the authorization server’s issuer origin (the platform origin).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### spec

the connector being verified — optional, so the AS itself can be
preflighted before any connector exists.

* **Type:**
  [`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### fetch

`fetch(url) -> parsed_json`; defaults to `fetch_json()`. Pass
your own to test offline, to add auth headers, or to use `httpx`.

* **Type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

The AS discovery document (fetched once per context, checked to be a doc).
