### enlace_connector.allowlist_users(spec)

`spec.allowed_users`, refused when it cannot mean what it seems to.

enlace_auth fails closed: a resource missing from
`[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` is refused to everyone
(i2mint/enlace_auth#34). So an empty list no longer means “open”. It
would deploy a connector that nobody can authorize, and nothing would
error until someone tried (#8). Opening a connector to every account is
an explicit `["*"]`.

```pycon
>>> from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec
>>> allowlist_users(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=["m:f"], allowed_users=["*"]))
['*']
>>> allowlist_users(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=["m:f"]))
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: Connector 'x' has no allowed_users...
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### enlace_connector.authorization_server_metadata(issuer, , fetch=None)

Fetch the RFC 8414 discovery document advertised by *issuer*.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### enlace_connector.chain_lifespan(app, extra_lifespan)

Run *extra_lifespan* inside *app*’s own lifespan, and return *app*.

*app* is a Starlette app (what `server.http_app(...)` returns); its own
lifespan runs FastMCP’s session manager, so an app wrapper that needs
startup/shutdown work must add to it, not replace it (see “Serving order” in
the module docstring). *extra_lifespan* is a Starlette lifespan: a callable
taking the app and returning an async context manager (an
`@asynccontextmanager` function), or an async generator function taking the
app, as Starlette’s `lifespan=` accepts. It starts after the app’s own
lifespan and stops before it, so the MCP endpoint is up for as long as the
extra work is. If either yields a state mapping, the two are merged (the
extra one wins on a shared key) into the request `scope["state"]`; that
needs an ASGI server with lifespan state (uvicorn has it).

```pycon
>>> from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
>>> from starlette.applications import Starlette
>>> @asynccontextmanager
... async def downloads(app):
...     yield {"signer": "ready"}
>>> app = chain_lifespan(Starlette(), downloads)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### enlace_connector.check_distinct_ports(specs)

Refuse *specs* that would bind the same local port.

`port` has a default, so two specs that both omit it render units that
collide on one box, and the second connector never starts (#15). Prefer
[`check_distinct_specs()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.check_distinct_specs), which also checks unit names and directories.

```pycon
>>> check_distinct_ports([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[], port=8031),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[], port=8032)])
>>> check_distinct_ports([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[]),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[])])
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: connectors share a port: 8030 (a, b)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.check_distinct_specs(specs)

Refuse *specs* that would collide on one host: same port, unit or directory.

Run it over every connector a host deploys. Two specs collide when they bind
the same `port` (it has a default), share a `name` (one
`<name>-mcp.service`, one resource URL), or share a directory under
`apps/` and `connectors/` (`app_dir`, else `name`): the second
install would overwrite the first (#18). Every clash is listed in one error.

```pycon
>>> check_distinct_specs([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[], port=8031),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[], port=8032)])
>>> check_distinct_specs([ConnectorSpec(name="a", tools=[], port=8031),
...                       ConnectorSpec(name="b", tools=[], port=8032, app_dir="a")])
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: connectors share a directory: a (a, b)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.check_jwks_uri_matches_convention(ctx)

For `auth="enlace"` connectors: the AS’s `jwks_uri` is the one we validate against.

Catches an issuer/route drift that would make every token fail signature
validation — a different symptom of “deployed, healthy, unusable”.

* **Return type:**
  [`CheckResult`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.CheckResult)

### enlace_connector.check_refresh_grant_supported(ctx)

THE check: does the AS advertise `refresh_token` in `grant_types_supported`?

An authorization server that omits it can only ever hand out access tokens that
expire into a dead end, which is invisible from the connector’s own health.

* **Return type:**
  [`CheckResult`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.CheckResult)

### enlace_connector.client_supports_sampling(ctx)

Whether the client behind *ctx* (a `fastmcp.Context`) advertises sampling.

`False` when it cannot be told (no session, an older SDK): the safe answer,
since the tool then runs on its fallback.

**Sampling needs a stateful session.** A connector served with
`stateless_http=True` (the `ConnectorSpec` default) builds a fresh
session per request that never saw the client’s `initialize`, so this is
always `False` there; set `stateless_http=False` on the spec for sampling.
That case is logged once, at info level, so it is not invisible.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### enlace_connector.diff_unit(spec, installed, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com', ignore=frozenset({('Unit', 'Description')}))

How the *installed* unit text differs from what *spec* renders; `[]` if not.

For a host that keeps its own unit files: run it per connector at deploy time
and report the lines, so a unit and its spec cannot drift apart unnoticed
(#15). The comparison is semantic: comments, blank lines, line order across
directives, whitespace runs and `Environment=` quoting do not count; the
order of repeated directives (`ExecStartPre=`) does. *ignore* is a set of
`(section, key)` pairs left out (the `Description=` prose, by default).
Drop-ins (`<unit>.d/*.conf`) are not read: pass the main unit file.

```pycon
>>> spec = ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], port=8040)
>>> diff_unit(spec, render_systemd_unit(spec))
[]
>>> diff_unit(spec, render_systemd_unit(spec).replace("8040", "8041"))[0][:21]
'[Service] ExecStart: '
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### enlace_connector.enlace_resource(, issuer, audience, scopes=('mcp:read',), mcp_path='/mcp')

Resource-server config validating tokens from the platform’s `enlace_auth` AS.

* **Parameters:**
  * **issuer** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the platform origin acting as the OAuth issuer, e.g.
    `"https://apps.thorwhalen.com"` (no trailing slash needed).
  * **audience** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – this connector’s **base** URL (e.g.
    `"https://apps.thorwhalen.com/api/trufflepig_mcp"`).
  * **scopes** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – scopes the connector requires (default `DFLT_SCOPES`).
  * **mcp_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the MCP transport sub-path (FastMCP default `/mcp`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The OAuth *resource* a connector validates is its MCP **endpoint**
(`base + mcp_path`) — that is what FastMCP advertises in the RFC 9728
protected-resource metadata, and therefore what the issued token’s `aud`
carries. So `base_url` (used to build that metadata) is the base, while the
validated `audience` is `base + mcp_path`. Setting them equal causes an
“audience mismatch” 401 at token-validation time.

### enlace_connector.format_report(results)

Render check results as a human-readable report (used by the CLI and errors).

```pycon
>>> print(format_report([CheckResult("a", True, "fine"),
...                      CheckResult("b", False, "broken", "fix it")]))
PASS  a: fine
FAIL  b: broken
      -> fix it
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.generate_deploy_bundle(spec, dest, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com', server_py=None, refresh_token_ttl_seconds=2592000)

Write the full deploy bundle for *spec* under *dest*.

Writes the app dir (`app.toml` + `server.py`) and a `deploy/` folder (the
systemd unit, provisioning script, the `platform.toml` fragments — OAuth
session longevity, the display name and the resource allowlist — and the
runbook). Raises `ValueError`, writing nothing, when `allowed_users` is
empty (see [`allowlist_users()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.allowlist_users)). Pass *server_py* to override the generated entry module
(e.g. a corpus-bound `make_search` server the composing skill wrote); pass
*refresh_token_ttl_seconds* to set the session longevity the platform fragment
configures (`0` would disable the refresh grant — see
[`render_oauth_server_toml()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.render_oauth_server_toml)). Returns the written paths.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

### enlace_connector.idp_resource(, jwks_uri, issuer, audience, authorization_servers=None, base_url=None, scopes=('mcp:read',))

Resource-server config validating tokens from an external managed IdP.

Everything is explicit because each IdP (Auth0, WorkOS, Okta…) publishes its
own `jwks_uri` / `issuer`. `authorization_servers` defaults to
`[issuer]` and `base_url` to `audience` (this connector’s URL).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### enlace_connector.llm_tool(fn=None, , llm_param='llm', fallback=None, use_sampling=True, \*\*sampling_kwargs)

Wrap a sync `fn(..., llm=None)` into an async MCP tool that brings its LLM.

Per request, the LLM is: a [`sampling_llm()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling_llm) when *use_sampling* and the
client advertises sampling; else *fallback* (a `prompt -> str`, or a
`"module:attr"` ref to one, resolved once, at wrap time); else `None`,
which `fn` must treat as “run offline”. If a sampling request fails while
`fn` runs, `fn` runs again with the fallback (or offline): the tool
answers either way. `fn` runs in a worker thread, so a slow search does not
block the server.

The rerun starts `fn` from the beginning, so `fn` must be safe to run
twice up to its first LLM call (a search is; a tool that writes before
asking the LLM is not). Only a failed sampling request triggers it, not a
[`SamplingUnavailable`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.SamplingUnavailable) that `fn` raises itself. A cancelled request
cannot stop the worker thread, but its next LLM call raises at once.

The tool’s signature is `fn`’s minus *llm_param*, plus `ctx` (which
FastMCP injects and hides from the client); name and docstring are `fn`’s.
`sampling_kwargs` go to [`sampling_llm()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling_llm) (`system_prompt`,
`max_tokens`, `temperature`, `timeout`). Usable bare or with arguments:
`@llm_tool` or `@llm_tool(fallback="mypkg.llm:chat")`.

### enlace_connector.make_connector_app(spec, , issuer=None, audience=None, settings=None, middleware=None)

Build the Streamable-HTTP ASGI app for *spec* (the hosted connector).

Resolves the spec’s `auth` into a py2mcp resource-server config. For
`auth="enlace"` provide *issuer* (the platform origin) and *audience* (this
connector’s public URL); if *audience* is omitted it is derived from *issuer* +
the spec’s route. Returns an ASGI app to run under any ASGI server (or mount in
enlace). The spec’s `icon`, `instructions`, `middleware`,
`server_hooks` and `app_wrappers` are applied, so a connector that needs
them is still built here rather than by hand (#3, #22). The order they are
applied in is “Serving order” in the module docstring.

Per-call usage logging is attached when the host’s *settings* (`os.environ`
by default) set `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR` — see [`enlace_connector.usage`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#module-enlace_connector.usage);
it is off otherwise; the spec’s `version` and `usage_outcome` feed it. Any
extra *middleware* (one or an ordered iterable) runs before the spec’s and the
logger, so a gate (e.g. `enlace_metering`) refuses a call before it is logged
as usage. Do not add a second `usage_middleware(...)` there: every call would
be recorded twice.

### enlace_connector.make_stdio_server(spec)

Build a FastMCP server for *spec*, for local stdio serving (no auth).

Use for `server.run()` in Claude Desktop / Claude Code while developing the
tools; the hosted path uses [`make_connector_app()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.make_connector_app). The spec’s `icon`,
`instructions` and `server_hooks` apply; its `middleware`, the
middleware its hooks return, and its `app_wrappers` do not (they are the
hosted path’s gating, metering and routes; see “Serving order” in the module
docstring).

### enlace_connector.render_allowlist_toml(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the `[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` fragment.

Maps this connector’s resource URL to the allowed emails (or `"*"`) —
paste into the platform’s `platform.toml`. Raises `ValueError` when
`allowed_users` is empty: see [`allowlist_users()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.allowlist_users).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_app_toml(spec, , port, command=None)

Render the enlace `app.toml` for *spec* as a `mode="process"` app.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_display_names_toml(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the `[auth.oauth_server.resource_display_names]` fragment.

The shared OAuth consent page (`enlace_auth`) shows *some* product name to
every user authorizing *any* connector on the platform — resolved from
`resource_display_names`, keyed by resource URL (see
[`resource_url()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.resource_url)), with a generic fallback when a resource has no entry.
Before this existed, that string had to be hand-typed once in platform
config and drifted the moment a second connector was added: every consent
screen showed the *first* connector’s name (i2mint/enlace_auth#18).

This makes [`ConnectorSpec.title`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.ConnectorSpec.title) the single source instead — paste the
fragment into the platform’s `platform.toml` alongside
[`render_allowlist_toml()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.render_allowlist_toml)’s.

```pycon
>>> from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec
>>> spec = ConnectorSpec(name="acme", tools=["m:f"], title="Acme Knowledge")
>>> print(render_display_names_toml(spec))
[auth.oauth_server.resource_display_names]
"https://apps.thorwhalen.com/acme-mcp/mcp" = "Acme Knowledge"
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_oauth_server_toml(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com', refresh_token_ttl_seconds=2592000)

Render the `[auth.oauth_server]` fragment that keeps sessions alive.

Companion to [`render_allowlist_toml()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.render_allowlist_toml): that one renders the
`[auth.oauth_server.resource_allowlist]` *subtable*, this one the scalar keys
of the parent table — so a **new** platform is configured for connector-length
sessions from the start instead of inheriting a default that issues no refresh
tokens. Paste this block *before* the allowlist fragment (TOML requires a
table’s own keys to precede its subtables).

```pycon
>>> from enlace_connector import ConnectorSpec
>>> spec = ConnectorSpec(name="acme", tools=["m:f"])
>>> print(render_oauth_server_toml(spec))
#...
[auth.oauth_server]
refresh_token_ttl_seconds = 2592000
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_provision_script(spec, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform')

Render the idempotent, run-as-root provisioning script for the connector.

Builds the dedicated venv (this box’s `ensurepip` is unavailable, so
`--without-pip` + `get-pip.py`, using the same base interpreter that made
the shared venv), installs `extras` + `git_installs`, creates the data
dirs, runs `post_install` (e.g. warm a model), and installs/starts the unit.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_runbook(spec, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the human deploy checklist (ship, provision, deploy, **verify**).

The last step is the one that is easy to skip and expensive to skip: a
connector whose authorization server cannot issue refresh tokens looks fully
deployed and dies silently hours later, so the runbook states that failure mode
in plain words and gives the exact command that detects it.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_server_py(spec)

Render the `server.py` that exposes `app` for enlace’s process runner.

The embedded `SPEC` carries every field `
make_connector_app()` reads at serve time — tools, auth, name/title, route,
`stateless_http`, and (when set) `icon`, `instructions`, `middleware`,
`server_hooks`, `app_wrappers`, `version`, `version_dist` and
`usage_outcome`.
A `"module:ATTR"` `instructions` or `version` is rendered as the ref,
not its value, so it is read from the installed package at serve time.

Deploy-time-only fields (`extras`, `git_installs`,
`data`, `env`, `post_install`, `allowed_users`) are deliberately
omitted: they are consumed by the provisioning bundle, not by the process.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.render_systemd_unit(spec, , remote_base='/opt/tw_platform', issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

Render the systemd unit that runs the connector in its own venv.

A host that hand-maintains its units can treat this as the reference: run
[`diff_unit()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.diff_unit) against each installed unit, so the two cannot drift apart
silently (#15). The spec carries what such units need: an `app_dir` name,
`environment_files` and `exec_start_pre` for scoped secrets,
`uvicorn_args`, and other `service_directives`.

`CONNECTOR_AUDIENCE` is rendered next to `CONNECTOR_ISSUER` by the same code
that renders the allowlist key, and [`render_server_py()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.render_server_py) passes it through
explicitly, so the runtime never re-derives it: a connector venv holding an older
`enlace_connector` (whose `mount_route` spelled the route differently) still
validates tokens for exactly the key the platform allows (#12).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.resolve_auth(auth, , issuer=None, audience=None)

Normalize an `auth` spec to a py2mcp auth dict (or `None` for no auth).

Accepts:

- `None` or `"none"` → unauthenticated (returns `None`).
- a ready auth dict → returned unchanged.
- `"enlace"` → [`enlace_resource()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.enlace_resource) (needs *issuer* and *audience*).
- `"idp"` → not resolvable from a bare string; pass an explicit dict from
  [`idp_resource()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.idp_resource) instead (raises with that guidance).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.resource_url(spec, , issuer='https://apps.thorwhalen.com')

The connector’s OAuth resource = its public MCP endpoint (`route + /mcp`).

The result is the allowlist key, so it must be canonical: enlace_auth refuses any
other spelling at config load. The route is normalized by
[`ConnectorSpec.mount_route`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.ConnectorSpec.mount_route); an issuer that is not canonical (an uppercase
host, a default port, a path segment that is empty or a dot) is refused here
rather than lowercased, because the same issuer is the connector’s runtime
`iss`/audience origin and must be fixed at its source (#10).

```pycon
>>> resource_url(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], route="/api/x_mcp/"))
'https://apps.thorwhalen.com/api/x_mcp/mcp'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.sampling_llm(ctx, , loop=None, system_prompt=None, max_tokens=1024, temperature=None, timeout=60.0, cancelled=None)

A sync `prompt -> str` that asks the client’s model through `ctx.sample`.

Create it inside the async tool (so *loop* defaults to the running one) and
call it from a worker thread, as [`llm_tool()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.llm_tool) does: it schedules the
request on *loop* and waits for the answer. Calling it on the loop’s own
thread would deadlock, so that raises `RuntimeError`. Any failure of the
request (the client does not sample, it refused, it timed out) raises
[`SamplingUnavailable`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.SamplingUnavailable). Once *cancelled* (an event the caller sets when
the request is abandoned) is set, every call raises at once, so a worker
thread left behind by a cancelled request stops at its next LLM call.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### enlace_connector.scaffold_app(spec, dest_dir, , port, command=None)

Write `app.toml` and `server.py` for *spec* into *dest_dir*.

*dest_dir* is the enlace app directory (e.g. `tw_platform/apps/<name>`).
Returns the paths written. Creates *dest_dir* if needed; overwrites the two
generated files (they are derived artifacts).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

### enlace_connector.spec_instructions(spec)

*spec*’s instructions, a `"module:ATTR"` ref resolved to its text.

```pycon
>>> spec_instructions(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], instructions="Use me."))
'Use me.'
>>> spec_instructions(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[],
...                                 instructions="string:ascii_lowercase"))[:3]
'abc'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.spec_version(spec)

*spec*’s version: `version` (a `"module:ATTR"` ref resolved), else the
installed version of `version_dist`, else `None`. The version is only a
label in the usage log, so a ref that does not import is kept as written and
an uninstalled `version_dist` gives `None`, each with a warning, rather
than stopping the connector at boot.

```pycon
>>> spec_version(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], version="1.2.0"))
'1.2.0'
>>> spec_version(ConnectorSpec(name="x", tools=[], version_dist="pytest")) > "0"
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### enlace_connector.usage_middleware(spec, , settings=None, version=None, \*\*logger_kwargs)

The usage-logging middleware for *spec*, or `[]` when it is switched off.

* **Parameters:**
  * **spec** ([`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec)) – the connector; its `name`, `version` and `usage_outcome` are
    carried into every record / the classifier.
  * **settings** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – where the `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_*` keys are read from
    (default `os.environ`). Pass a dict to configure in code or tests.
  * **version** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – overrides `spec.version` for the records.
  * **\*\*logger_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – forwarded to `py2mcp.usage.UsageLogger` (e.g. a
    `sink=` for tests, or an `outcome=` callable). They override what
    the settings and the spec imply. Passing a `sink` switches logging
    on even without `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR`.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)
* **Returns:**
  A one-element list (the `UsageLogger`) when logging is on, else `[]` —
  always something `middleware=` accepts.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – a setting is malformed (a relative log dir, a non-integer
      retention, an unrecognised yes/no). Loud at boot on purpose: these
      are configuration mistakes, not runtime conditions.

### enlace_connector.verify_deployment(spec=None, \*, issuer, checks=(<function check_refresh_grant_supported>, <function check_jwks_uri_matches_convention>), fetch=None, strict=False)

Run the preflight checks against *issuer*; return one result per check.

This is the “is this deployment actually good?” gate — run it after deploying a
connector (and, ideally, before), because the most consequential property of the
platform is one the connector cannot observe about itself.

* **Parameters:**
  * **spec** ([`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the connector being verified (optional — the AS can be checked alone).
  * **issuer** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the authorization server / platform origin.
  * **checks** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`PreflightContext`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.PreflightContext)], [`CheckResult`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.CheckResult)]]) – the checks to run (defaults to `DFLT_CHECKS`).
  * **fetch** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]) – `fetch(url) -> parsed_json` seam (defaults to `fetch_json()`).
  * **strict** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – raise [`PreflightError`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.html.md#enlace_connector.PreflightError) if any check fails.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`CheckResult`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.CheckResult)]

```pycon
>>> md = {"grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code"]}
>>> results = verify_deployment(issuer="https://p.example.com",
...                             fetch=lambda url: md)
>>> [r.name for r in results if not r]
['oauth_refresh_grant', 'oauth_jwks_uri']
```

# _autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md

# enlace_connector.preflight

Preflight/verify checks — is the target platform able to keep a connector *alive*?

A connector deployment can be perfectly healthy and still be **dead to its users**.
The failure this module exists to catch: the platform’s OAuth 2.1 authorization
server issues a short-lived access token and **no refresh token** (it does not
advertise `refresh_token` in `grant_types_supported`). Every client session then
hard-dies at the first token expiry — while the connector process stays green,
the port answers, and nothing errors anywhere. The only recovery is a human
re-running the interactive browser authorization, and the stock 401 challenge text
actively misinforms by claiming the client can renew on its own.

Nothing about the connector bundle can detect that from the inside, so it is a
*preflight of the authorization server*: fetch the AS’s discovery document at
`{issuer}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and assert what it advertises.

Run it as a function, or from the shell:

```default
python -m enlace_connector.preflight https://apps.example.com
```

Checks are plain callables of a [`PreflightContext`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.PreflightContext), so a platform with extra
requirements passes its own `checks=` sequence to [`verify_deployment()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.verify_deployment)
without this module knowing about them. The HTTP fetcher is likewise a parameter
([`fetch_json()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.fetch_json) by default — stdlib only), which is what makes the whole thing
testable offline:

```pycon
>>> md = {"grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
...       "jwks_uri": "https://p.example.com/auth/oauth/jwks"}
>>> ctx = PreflightContext(issuer="https://p.example.com", fetch=lambda url: md)
>>> check_refresh_grant_supported(ctx).ok
True
>>> print(check_refresh_grant_supported(ctx).summary)
authorization server advertises the refresh_token grant
```

A server missing the grant fails loudly, with the remedy attached:

```pycon
>>> stale = PreflightContext(issuer="https://p.example.com",
...                          fetch=lambda url: {"grant_types_supported":
...                                             ["authorization_code"]})
>>> result = check_refresh_grant_supported(stale)
>>> bool(result)
False
>>> print(result.summary)
authorization server does NOT advertise the refresh_token grant...
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **spec** ([`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the connector being verified (optional — the AS can be checked alone).
  * **issuer** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the authorization server / platform origin.
  * **checks** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`PreflightContext`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.PreflightContext)], [`CheckResult`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.CheckResult)]]) – the checks to run (defaults to [`DFLT_CHECKS`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.DFLT_CHECKS)).
  * **fetch** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]) – `fetch(url) -> parsed_json` seam (defaults to [`fetch_json()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.fetch_json)).
  * **strict** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – raise [`PreflightError`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.PreflightError) if any check fails.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`CheckResult`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.preflight.html.md#enlace_connector.preflight.CheckResult)]

```pycon
>>> md = {"grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code"]}
>>> results = verify_deployment(issuer="https://p.example.com",
...                             fetch=lambda url: md)
>>> [r.name for r in results if not r]
['oauth_refresh_grant', 'oauth_jwks_uri']
```


# _autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md

# enlace_connector.sampling

Run a connector tool’s LLM on the client’s model (MCP sampling), offline otherwise.

An *agentic* connector tool (query reformulation, LLM selection, a synopsis) needs
a `prompt -> str` callable. MCP *sampling* lets the server ask the connected
client’s model instead of a metered key: FastMCP exposes it as `ctx.sample`.
This module turns that into the sync callable the tool’s seams take, and makes
the tool degrade instead of fail when the client cannot sample.

**Client support (checked 2026-10).** Claude’s own MCP client (claude.ai,
Desktop, mobile, Cowork, Claude Code) lists sampling among the features it does
*not* yet support, so under Claude the tool runs on its fallback: a configured
`prompt -> str` (a key, or `coact.resolve_llm()` on a developer machine), or
no LLM at all (offline). Clients that advertise `sampling` get it with no code
change. Re-check when Claude’s connector docs change.

- [`client_supports_sampling()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.client_supports_sampling) — does this request’s client advertise it?
- [`sampling_llm()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.sampling_llm) — a sync `prompt -> str` over `ctx.sample`, to call
  from a worker thread (the tool’s seams are sync, the server loop is not).
- [`llm_tool()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.llm_tool) — wrap a sync `fn(..., llm=None)` into an async tool that
  picks the LLM per request (sampling, else *fallback*, else `None`), runs
  `fn` off the event loop, and retries on the fallback if sampling fails
  mid-call. The connector never hard-fails for want of an LLM.

```pycon
>>> def search(query: str, *, llm=None) -> str:
...     return query.upper() if llm is None else llm(query)
>>> tool = llm_tool(search)
>>> [p for p in tool.__signature__.parameters]
['query', 'ctx']
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MAX_TOKENS`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.DFLT_MAX_TOKENS)         | `max_tokens` of one sampling request (FastMCP's own default is 512, short for a synopsis).                                            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_SAMPLING_TIMEOUT_S`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.DFLT_SAMPLING_TIMEOUT_S) | seconds one sampling request may take before it counts as unavailable; well under the 240 s a Claude client allows a whole tool call. |

### Functions

| [`client_supports_sampling`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.client_supports_sampling)(ctx)                     | Whether the client behind *ctx* (a `fastmcp.Context`) advertises sampling.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`sampling_llm`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.sampling_llm)(ctx, \*[, loop, system_prompt, ...]) | A sync `prompt -> str` that asks the client's model through `ctx.sample`.    |
| [`llm_tool`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.llm_tool)([fn, llm_param, fallback, use_sampling]) | Wrap a sync `fn(..., llm=None)` into an async MCP tool that brings its LLM.  |

### Exceptions

| [`SamplingUnavailable`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.SamplingUnavailable)   | The client cannot (or did not) answer a sampling request.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|

### enlace_connector.sampling.DFLT_MAX_TOKENS *= 1024*

`max_tokens` of one sampling request (FastMCP’s own default is 512, short
for a synopsis).

### enlace_connector.sampling.DFLT_SAMPLING_TIMEOUT_S *= 60.0*

seconds one sampling request may take before it counts as unavailable;
well under the 240 s a Claude client allows a whole tool call.

### *exception* enlace_connector.sampling.SamplingUnavailable

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

The client cannot (or did not) answer a sampling request.

### enlace_connector.sampling.client_supports_sampling(ctx)

Whether the client behind *ctx* (a `fastmcp.Context`) advertises sampling.

`False` when it cannot be told (no session, an older SDK): the safe answer,
since the tool then runs on its fallback.

**Sampling needs a stateful session.** A connector served with
`stateless_http=True` (the `ConnectorSpec` default) builds a fresh
session per request that never saw the client’s `initialize`, so this is
always `False` there; set `stateless_http=False` on the spec for sampling.
That case is logged once, at info level, so it is not invisible.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### enlace_connector.sampling.llm_tool(fn=None, , llm_param='llm', fallback=None, use_sampling=True, \*\*sampling_kwargs)

Wrap a sync `fn(..., llm=None)` into an async MCP tool that brings its LLM.

Per request, the LLM is: a [`sampling_llm()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.sampling_llm) when *use_sampling* and the
client advertises sampling; else *fallback* (a `prompt -> str`, or a
`"module:attr"` ref to one, resolved once, at wrap time); else `None`,
which `fn` must treat as “run offline”. If a sampling request fails while
`fn` runs, `fn` runs again with the fallback (or offline): the tool
answers either way. `fn` runs in a worker thread, so a slow search does not
block the server.

The rerun starts `fn` from the beginning, so `fn` must be safe to run
twice up to its first LLM call (a search is; a tool that writes before
asking the LLM is not). Only a failed sampling request triggers it, not a
[`SamplingUnavailable`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.SamplingUnavailable) that `fn` raises itself. A cancelled request
cannot stop the worker thread, but its next LLM call raises at once.

The tool’s signature is `fn`’s minus *llm_param*, plus `ctx` (which
FastMCP injects and hides from the client); name and docstring are `fn`’s.
`sampling_kwargs` go to [`sampling_llm()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.sampling_llm) (`system_prompt`,
`max_tokens`, `temperature`, `timeout`). Usable bare or with arguments:
`@llm_tool` or `@llm_tool(fallback="mypkg.llm:chat")`.

### enlace_connector.sampling.sampling_llm(ctx, , loop=None, system_prompt=None, max_tokens=1024, temperature=None, timeout=60.0, cancelled=None)

A sync `prompt -> str` that asks the client’s model through `ctx.sample`.

Create it inside the async tool (so *loop* defaults to the running one) and
call it from a worker thread, as [`llm_tool()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.llm_tool) does: it schedules the
request on *loop* and waits for the answer. Calling it on the loop’s own
thread would deadlock, so that raises `RuntimeError`. Any failure of the
request (the client does not sample, it refused, it timed out) raises
[`SamplingUnavailable`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.sampling.html.md#enlace_connector.sampling.SamplingUnavailable). Once *cancelled* (an event the caller sets when
the request is abandoned) is set, every call raises at once, so a worker
thread left behind by a cancelled request stops at its next LLM call.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/enlace_connector.scaffold.html.md

# enlace_connector.scaffold

Generate the enlace app directory that serves a connector.

A connector with heavy dependencies (ML models, large libraries) should not be
mounted in-process with the rest of the platform — it runs as an enlace
`mode="process"` app: enlace spawns it as a supervised subprocess in its \*\*own
venv\*\* and reverse-proxies the route to it. This module renders that app dir — an
`app.toml` (access=public, mode=process, route) and a `server.py` that builds
the connector app from its [`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec).

The connector authenticates clients itself (bearer JWTs), so at the enlace layer it
is `access="public"` — enlace does not gate it with session cookies.

### Functions

| [`render_app_toml`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.scaffold.html.md#enlace_connector.scaffold.render_app_toml)(spec, \*, port[, command])        | Render the enlace `app.toml` for *spec* as a `mode="process"` app.     |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`render_server_py`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.scaffold.html.md#enlace_connector.scaffold.render_server_py)(spec)                            | Render the `server.py` that exposes `app` for enlace's process runner. |
| [`scaffold_app`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.scaffold.html.md#enlace_connector.scaffold.scaffold_app)(spec, dest_dir, \*, port[, command]) | Write `app.toml` and `server.py` for *spec* into *dest_dir*.           |

### enlace_connector.scaffold.render_app_toml(spec, , port, command=None)

Render the enlace `app.toml` for *spec* as a `mode="process"` app.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.scaffold.render_server_py(spec)

Render the `server.py` that exposes `app` for enlace’s process runner.

The embedded `SPEC` carries every field `
make_connector_app()` reads at serve time — tools, auth, name/title, route,
`stateless_http`, and (when set) `icon`, `instructions`, `middleware`,
`server_hooks`, `app_wrappers`, `version`, `version_dist` and
`usage_outcome`.
A `"module:ATTR"` `instructions` or `version` is rendered as the ref,
not its value, so it is read from the installed package at serve time.

Deploy-time-only fields (`extras`, `git_installs`,
`data`, `env`, `post_install`, `allowed_users`) are deliberately
omitted: they are consumed by the provisioning bundle, not by the process.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_connector.scaffold.scaffold_app(spec, dest_dir, , port, command=None)

Write `app.toml` and `server.py` for *spec* into *dest_dir*.

*dest_dir* is the enlace app directory (e.g. `tw_platform/apps/<name>`).
Returns the paths written. Creates *dest_dir* if needed; overwrites the two
generated files (they are derived artifacts).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]


# _autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md

# enlace_connector.usage

Switch a connector’s per-call usage log on by configuration alone.

The mechanism is `py2mcp.usage.UsageLogger` (one record per tool call and
per handshake, to a sink). *Whether* a given deployed connector keeps that log,
*where*, for *how long*, and with *which arguments redacted* are host decisions,
so they are read here from one settings mapping — `os.environ` by default,
which is what a systemd unit’s `Environment=` lines populate — and never
written into connector code:

- `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR` — the directory for the day files, **absolute**,
  one per connector. **Unset = off** (the default). Point it at the connector’s
  own data root, off the deploy tree, e.g. `<connectors>/<name>/data/usage`. A
  relative path or `~` is refused: the unit’s working directory is the deploy
  tree, which is exactly where users’ questions must never land.
- `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` — days of files to keep (default
  [`DFLT_RETENTION_DAYS`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#enlace_connector.usage.DFLT_RETENTION_DAYS); `0` keeps today only; `none` keeps everything).
- `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_REDACT` — comma-separated argument names whose values
  are replaced before the record is written (error text is then dropped too).
- `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_ARGS` — `0`/`false` to drop the arguments entirely
  (keeping caller, tool, outcome, size and latency); anything other than a
  yes/no value is refused.

The spec’s `version` and `usage_outcome` (a `"module:function"` ref to the
connector’s own outcome classifier) are carried into the logger, so a connector
that knows its search tool’s “no match” shape declares that once, in its spec.

[`usage_middleware()`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#enlace_connector.usage.usage_middleware) returns the list to pass as `middleware=` — empty when
logging is off, so a connector can wire it unconditionally:

```default
server = FastMCP(SPEC.server_name, auth=..., middleware=usage_middleware(SPEC))
```

`make_connector_app()` does this already. The arguments are the users’ own
questions: turn this on for a client-facing connector only after telling them.
See py2mcp’s ADR-0001 (`misc/docs/decisions/0001-usage-logging-is-a-py2mcp-middleware.md`).

```pycon
>>> usage_middleware(ConnectorSpec(name="demo", tools=[]), settings={})
[]
>>> import tempfile
>>> (mw,) = usage_middleware(
...     ConnectorSpec(name="demo", tools=[]),
...     settings={"CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR": tempfile.mkdtemp(),
...               "CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_REDACT": "api_key, token"},
... )
>>> mw.name, sorted(mw.redact), mw.sink.retention_days
('demo', ['api_key', 'token'], 90)
```

### Module Attributes

| [`USAGE_LOG_DIR`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#enlace_connector.usage.USAGE_LOG_DIR)       | Settings keys (environment variable names in the common case).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_RETENTION_DAYS`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#enlace_connector.usage.DFLT_RETENTION_DAYS) | Default retention, in days, when the setting is absent.          |

### Functions

| [`usage_middleware`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.usage.html.md#enlace_connector.usage.usage_middleware)(spec, \*[, settings, version])   | The usage-logging middleware for *spec*, or `[]` when it is switched off.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### enlace_connector.usage.DFLT_RETENTION_DAYS *= 90*

Default retention, in days, when the setting is absent.

### enlace_connector.usage.USAGE_LOG_DIR *= 'CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR'*

Settings keys (environment variable names in the common case).

### enlace_connector.usage.usage_middleware(spec, , settings=None, version=None, \*\*logger_kwargs)

The usage-logging middleware for *spec*, or `[]` when it is switched off.

* **Parameters:**
  * **spec** ([`ConnectorSpec`](_autosummary/enlace_connector.connector.html.md#enlace_connector.connector.ConnectorSpec)) – the connector; its `name`, `version` and `usage_outcome` are
    carried into every record / the classifier.
  * **settings** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – where the `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_*` keys are read from
    (default `os.environ`). Pass a dict to configure in code or tests.
  * **version** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – overrides `spec.version` for the records.
  * **\*\*logger_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – forwarded to `py2mcp.usage.UsageLogger` (e.g. a
    `sink=` for tests, or an `outcome=` callable). They override what
    the settings and the spec imply. Passing a `sink` switches logging
    on even without `CONNECTOR_USAGE_LOG_DIR`.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)
* **Returns:**
  A one-element list (the `UsageLogger`) when logging is on, else `[]` —
  always something `middleware=` accepts.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – a setting is malformed (a relative log dir, a non-integer
      retention, an unrecognised yes/no). Loud at boot on purpose: these
      are configuration mistakes, not runtime conditions.

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`enlace_connector` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `corpus-connector`

Turn an ir corpus into a deployed, access-controlled MCP connector for a client. Use when the user wants to “make a connector for a corpus”, “deploy an ir corpus as a Claude connector”, “create a search connector for <client>”, “index these sources and expose them to Claude”, or “give <client> a searchable knowledge connector”. Composes ir (index/search) → py2mcp (functions→MCP) → enlace_connector (deploy any MCP connector) → the tw_platform server, and sets per-connector access control. The per-corpus work is config (a name + sources), not code.

Source: [`.claude/skills/corpus-connector`](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace_connector/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/corpus-connector).

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://i2mint.github.io/enlace_connector/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`enlace_connector.md`](https://i2mint.github.io/enlace_connector/enlace_connector.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://i2mint.github.io/enlace_connector/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)

# API reference
